title: Sell Mineral Rights in Monongahela, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Monongahela, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Monongahela, PA (Mon City) mineral owners: we buy Washington County interests directly along the river, with a full title review before any offer.
heroLead: Locals still call it Mon City, and this old river town in Washington County has watched more than one industry boom and fade along its banks, coal, steel, and now natural gas.
intro: Monongahela sits right on the river it's named for, and the surrounding townships have been part of Washington County's Marcellus development for well over a decade. If your family has owned ground near the city, whether it's still farmed or was sold off for other use long ago, there's a reasonable chance a mineral interest is tied to it that you haven't thought much about.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Monongahela directly. We do the deed research ourselves through the county recorder and walk you through what we find before ever discussing a number.

sections.heading: A River Town's Layered Mineral History
paragraphs: Like other Mon Valley towns, Monongahela's ground carries a coal-mining past that sometimes shows up as reservation language in older deeds. Confirming whether your oil and gas rights were caught up in an old coal transaction, or kept separate, is one of the first things we check.

Washington County remains one of the most heavily leased counties in the entire Marcellus play, and the wet-gas production here means liquids revenue is part of the value picture along with the processing deductions that come with it.

sections.heading: Confirming Your Interest Through County Records
paragraphs: We pull your title history from the Washington County Recorder of Deeds and check it against your current division order to confirm the decimal interest you're being paid matches what your deed actually supports.
If there's a discrepancy, we'll tell you before moving forward rather than letting it surface later.

sections.heading: What Post-Production Deductions Look Like Here
paragraphs: Older leases around Monongahela sometimes predate stronger royalty protections, so gathering and compression costs can take a larger bite than a newer lease would allow. Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act sets a floor, and we'll help you understand how your specific lease measures against it.

faqs.question: Does Monongahela's coal history complicate my gas rights?
faqs.answer: It can, since coal was frequently severed separately from oil and gas in this area. We check your specific deed rather than assuming either way.

faqs.question: Is my interest affected by being close to the river?
faqs.answer: Proximity to the river itself doesn't affect mineral value, though it can factor into surface access considerations for the operator, which we account for when relevant.

faqs.question: What should I send you to get started?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease documents, and recent royalty statements if you have them. That's enough for us to begin the review.
